findings.summary: The credit guard's own comment says "WROTE THE LEASE BACK" -- the exact claim the accessor's javadoc 38 lines below retracts as false. New this round.
findings.detail: Line 63 now reads '// ⚠️ THE RELEASE THAT WROTE THE LEASE BACK, not the branch that was entered, not merely a call that returned, and not merely a call that reached the store.' Line 101-110 says the opposite about the same guard: 'Releases that returned AND issued the conditional write. ⚠️ "ISSUED", NOT "WROTE". LeaseManager.releaseLocked DISCARDS the Optional its putIfMatch returns ... so a fenced leader completes, is credited here, and changed nothing on the store.' Verified in production: LeaseManager.releaseLocked calls store.putIfMatch(key, ..., mine.version()) with the result unassigned, and release()'s javadoc says the call is 'harmless when already fenced, because the conditional write simply loses'. The counter the guard reads (FaultInjectingStore.record at the top of putIfMatch) also moves for a CAS that loses, for a partition refusal, and for the withheldPut arm -- none of which write anything. This is a NEW false sentence: the text it replaced ('THE RELEASE THAT REACHED THE STORE') was true of the guard it described. Failure scenario: a later hand reads the guard, takes gracefulReleases (floor 1,000, measured 1,608) as a count of leases actually expired on the store, and argues from it that successors in the sweep never wait out a TTL -- an argument the javadoc below explicitly forbids. Fix is the two words at the head of the comment; do not touch the javadoc, which is correct.
findings.failure_scenario: A later hand reads the guard comment, takes gracefulReleases (floor 1,000, measured 1,608) as a count of leases that were actually written back and expired on the store, and argues from it that no successor in the sweep waits out a TTL -- while the accessor's own javadoc 38 lines below says a fenced leader is credited having changed nothing. One of the two sentences will be believed and it is a coin toss which.

findings.summary: "124 windows per 1,000 seeds already write the lease and THEN THROW -- the injected ambiguous putIfMatch" attributes the whole delta to one arm; two other arms of putIfMatch throw after `record` having written nothing, and both are enabled in the sweep.
findings.detail: The 1,732-minus-1,608 delta is every window where calls("putIfMatch") moved and `completed` was false. FaultInjectingStore.putIfMatch (sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/FaultInjectingStore.java:594-643) records at the top and can then throw from THREE places, not one: (a) refuseIfPartitioned() at line 624 -- nothing written; (b) the ambiguousPut arm -- write lands; (c) the withheldPut arm, whose own comment says 'THE VERSION DOES NOT MOVE ... nothing landed'. The sweep runs Faults(0.03, 0.03, 0.1, 0.02, 0.02, 0.02) (CommitProtocolSweepTest.java:97), so withheldPut fires at 2% of these calls and partitionRate is 0.02 -- and the sweep's own measured refusalsSeen is 38 windows per 1,000 seeds, all of them (refusedForAnotherPod asserted 0) the leader's own partition refusing its own release, which for a non-ambiguous belief is refused AT the putIfMatch. So on the diff's own numbers roughly 38 partition-refused plus ~2% withheld of ~1,700 calls wrote nothing: at most about half of the 124 'write the lease and then throw'. Same sentence at sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:222 ('**124 windows per 1,000 seeds already write the lease and then throw**. That is the injected ambiguous putIfMatch'), inherited at :264 ('the mechanism behind the sweep's 124 windows') and at :271 ('the 124 windows would stop being counted at all' -- only the ambiguous subset would). Failure scenario: a later hand tightening the sweep reads 124 as the ambiguous-landing rate and either floors an ambiguous-landing counter near 124 (the tree can only reach roughly half that, so the floor reds with no defect), or argues the M5.25/TTL point -- 'the lease really is expired on the store, so a successor does not wait out the TTL' (GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:227) -- for all 124 windows when in the withheld and partition ones the version never moved and the successor must wait the full TTL. Correction is one clause: name the delta as ambiguous-landing PLUS refused PLUS withheld, or drop the attribution.
findings.failure_scenario: A later hand tightening the sweep reads 124 as the ambiguous-landing rate: either a new floor near 124 for ambiguous landings reds with no defect present (the tree reaches roughly half that, the rest being partition-refused and withheldPut windows where the version never moved), or the TTL argument at GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:227 -- 'the lease really is expired on the store, so a successor does not wait out the TTL' -- is extended to all 124 windows, when in the withheld and partition ones the successor must wait the full TTL.

findings.detail: Position above the injected throw / above refuseIfPartitioned is pinned by three cases, not two: GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:107-111 (calls("stat") == 1 on a partition-REFUSED call, i.e. record above refuseIfPartitioned), GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:140-144 (calls("list") == 1 with the injected unreachable firing first, i.e. record above the throw) and theStoresOWNAmbiguousWriteIsCOUNTEDAndStillNotCredited (calls("putIfMatch") == 1 above the ambiguous throw). The rest of the row -- the grep over @Override in one file being rung 3, the M0.108 shape, presence-versus-position -- checks out: all twelve @Override methods in FaultInjectingStore.java now carry a record(...) call. Failure scenario: whoever takes M5.49 reads the row as saying nothing pins `list`, deletes the :140-144 assertion as redundant to the gate, and the one verb whose record sits above an injected throw rather than above refuseIfPartitioned loses its only position pin.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever takes M5.49 reads the row as saying nothing pins `list`, deletes the calls("list") assertion at GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:140-144 as redundant to the new grep gate, and the one verb whose record sits above an injected throw rather than above refuseIfPartitioned loses its only position pin -- so record("list") could be moved below the unreachable throw with the suite green.

findings.summary: New javadoc states in the present tense that GracefulReleaseMeter 'leans on this store to mean "the release did store work"' -- which this same commit made false.
findings.detail: After this diff the meter reads calls("putIfMatch") and means 'issued the conditional write'; every other sentence in the javadoc is correctly in the measured past ('review MEASURED that replacing ... left the sweep's floor green'). A reader arriving at theMeterNamesTheVERBAndNotMerelyTheCOUNT is told the current meter credits any store call and may reinstate that rule believing it is the status quo -- the precise hole GracefulReleaseMeter.released()'s third paragraph exists to close. Past tense ('used to lean') fixes it.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader arriving at theMeterNamesTheVERBAndNotMerelyTheCOUNT is told in the present tense that the meter credits any call that reached the store, reinstates that rule believing it is the status quo, and re-opens the hole this commit closed -- the one where leases.release() can be swapped for a stat with the sweep's floor green at 1,626.
